messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

function.name: genetics_get_variant_frequency

message.content: In male lions, the presence of a mane is a classic example of a dominant genetic trait. The gene that promotes mane growth is expressed whenever it is present, so even if a male lion inherits only one copy of the mane‑promoting allele (from either parent), he will develop a mane. This dominant trait is what gives male lions their distinctive, often impressive, fur around the head and neck.
